extracted.intended_audience: Heads of Executive Departments and Establishments; agency managers responsible for Federal parking
extracted.subtask_description: Draft OMB circular proposing a nationwide Federal employee parking policy: establish parking fees tied to commercial rental value, encourage carpooling/transit, require agency plans where parking remains free, and prescribe implementation details including a phase-in and comment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish parking fee based on fair monthly rental value
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular would establish a parking fee at all Federal installations based on the fair monthly rental value of the parking space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent is to set a fee high enough to recover space costs and act as an incentive to carpooling, yet not so low that administration of a fee system and parking management would totally consume the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-fee threshold: rental value under $10/month
rubrics_metrics.description: Except that in most cases no fee will be charged where the rental value is less than $10.00 per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This numeric threshold is an explicit exemption from charging; combined with the phase-in, it limits application where rental value is minimal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set fee to recover space costs and incentivize carpooling
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent is to set a fee high enough to recover space costs and act as an incentive to carpooling, yet not so low that administration of a fee system and parking management would totally consume the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance pricing to both recover costs and change employee behavior; avoid administrative overhead that outweighs fee revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in period for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular provides for a phase-in period to help employees and agencies adjust carpooling and financial arrangements as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use phased implementation to allow employees and agencies time to organize carpooling/vanpooling and adjust financially; no specific phase-in duration given in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency affirmative plans where parking remains free
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency managers at locations which would continue to provide parking without charge will be required to develop and implement affirmative plans for maximizing carpooling and vanpooling among employees and other building tenants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where agencies opt to continue free parking, they must still actively pursue carpool/vanpool programs and management actions to reduce single-occupant driving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize pricing in downtown and densely populated suburban locations
rubrics_metrics.description: The pricing policy will primarily affect Federal facilities in downtown locations and densely populated suburban locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus application where commercial-equivalent fees are most likely to reduce car trips and where parking rental value is significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply more stringent carpooling requirements government-wide
rubrics_metrics.description: More stringent application of carpooling requirements will affect all locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carpooling standards (e.g., utilization targets) should be applied broadly even if pricing is concentrated in core/dense areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy rationale: discourage subsidized employee parking
rubrics_metrics.description: In an increasingly energy-conscious era, it does not seem prudent for the nation's largest employer to subsidize employee parking; the Federal government's historical in-house practice of subsidizing parking costs for some employees has become inconsistent with more recent national policies toward energy conservation, reliance on public transportation and a cleaner environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these environmental, energy conservation, congestion, and equity rationales to justify pricing and carpooling measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical support: charge commercially equivalent fees to change behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on studies which relate automobile use to the cost of parking, the Washington Metropolitan Area Council of Governments has concluded that charging commercially equivalent fees for parking would reduce the number of cars in the core of the Washington, D.C. region. A comparative study of Federal and county employees in Los Angeles also supports the conclusion that where the user pays for parking, carpooling and transit use are increased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on comparative studies as evidence that pricing raises carpooling and transit use; use such evidence in implementation decisions and to set fee levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carpool utilization target (regulatory objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation's objective of 90 percent utilization by carpools (noted as an objective in the memo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo cites a 90% carpool utilization objective for core areas but notes surveys showing actual utilization is lower; use this target as a benchmark for agency plans and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit written comments by specified deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: We invite your written comments and ask that they be sent to Ms. Joyce Walker, Deputy Associate Director, Room 9202, OMB, Washington, D.C. 20503, no later than April 30, 1979.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement for the draft circular's notice-and-comment: direct responses to the named OMB contact by the deadline to participate in rule development.
